messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate and latency spike detected for /v1/generate on shard mistral-qwen-7 (kv-cache + cont-batch) :warning:
alicia: saw it on dashboards too, 5xxs up and tail latency spiking. paging oncall.
marcus: on my way, tail looks like huge queueing around cont-batch flushes. could be mem growth in kv cache.
jyoti: confirming increased KV cache evictions + OOMs on a couple replicas. logs show repetitive `kv_put` for long prefixes.
tom: adding context — we rolled cont-batch tuning 12h ago for MQA traffic to reduce 99p latency, maybe regressed with recent model variant weights.
alicia: customer impact? sara-cs, any reports?
sara-cs: just one Enterprise customer reported timeouts in their app, CS alerted billing & eng. No major data loss reported.
ryan: quick mitigation: can we disable continuous batching for mistral-qwen-7 via runtime flag? rollback to per-request batching for that shard.
marcus: yes we can. preparing config patch. will push a canary to 2 replicas first.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback cont-batch flag on cluster mistral-qwen-7 -> target=2 canary replicas, requester=marcus.
ops-bot: note: evicting large prefix entries might spikily increase miss rate. prefer rapid config change first.
marcus: canary applied to 2 replicas. monitoring.
alicia: metrics update?
jyoti: canary shows immediate drop in p95 and errors on those replicas. overall cluster error rate down 30% but still above baseline.
marcus: rolling patch to all replicas now.
deploy-bot: rollout to 10/10 replicas in progress -> status: 60%
alicia: while rollout completes, can we prime fallback model for critical customer? set routing policy to fallback to llama-small-quant on failures.
ryan: routing updated for customer prod-42 to prefer llama-small-quant when mistral-qwen returns >=5% errors. policy pushed.
sara-cs: letting customer know we routed their traffic to fallback and reduced timeout from 30s -> 10s, their app is partially recovered.
marcus: rollout complete. metrics back near normal for majority of traffic. still seeing occasional cont-batch oscillations on mixed GQA/MQA workloads.
jyoti: root cause hypoth: mismatch between MQA-aware batching heuristics and updated mistral tokenization causing long continuous prefixes that bloat KV cache; cont-batch flush policy hit worst-case and caused eviction storms.
marcus: created quick hotfix: limit continuous batch prefix length and add aggressive prefix-ttl for suspicious prefixes. snippet below:

```
cont_batch_max_prefix_len: 64
kv_prefix_ttl_sec: 60
kv_eviction_threshold_pct: 0.75
```

alicia: hotfix applied to cluster, monitoring. early signal: reduced kv_put rate and evictions normalized.
ops-bot: NOTE: this hotfix increases miss rate for some long-context flows; track regen with eval set.
ryan: we should also add a canary eval harness for GQA edge prompts that previously produced long prefixes. logging created: `gqa-prefix-eval`
marcus: assigning follow-ups: postmortem owner = jyoti, action items: (1) add prefix-cardinality telemetry per model variant, (2) improve cont-batch safety nets, (3) model-onboarding checklist add tokenization compatibility.
jyoti: ack, will start doc and timeline. planning 72h postmortem draft.
sara-cs: I'll draft customer-facing summary and coordinate HS-notify for impacted tenant list.
alicia: oncall handoff in 2h — @oncall-next please pick up monitoring and the customer list.
oncall-next: taking handoff. will check playbook and escalate if regressions return.
marcus: final note: no code-level model change deployed — this was config/runtime tuning. recommend pausing any MQA batching experiments until we have telemetry updates. :memo: 
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error rate and latency returned to acceptable range after cont-batch rollback + prefix-ttl hotfix. Postmortem assigned.
